caption:
OpenAI and Anthropic both publish official prompting guides.
Three tips stand out: tell the AI why a rule matters, say what to do instead of what to avoid, and ask it to check its own work.

Which one will you try first?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Anthropic, OpenAI · Photos: The Next Web, Zac Wolff / Unsplash

slides.headline: 3 prompt tricks *OpenAI and Anthropic* recommend in their own official guides

slides.heading: 1. Tell it *why*
paras: Don't just give a rule, add the reason. Anthropic's guide says explaining why something matters helps Claude understand the goal and apply it better.

paras.t: Example: "This will be read aloud by a text-to-speech engine, so never use ellipses."

slides.heading: 2. Say what to do, *not what to avoid*
paras: Both guides agree that clear instructions beat bans. Instead of "Do not use markdown," Anthropic suggests asking for "smoothly flowing prose paragraphs."
OpenAI adds: swap vague words for exact ones. "Write exactly two sentences" works better than "Keep it short."

slides.heading: 3. Make it *check its own work*
paras: Anthropic recommends ending a prompt with a self-check. It says verification catches errors, especially in coding and math.

paras.t: Try: "Before you finish, verify your answer against these criteria."

slides.hook: Save this for your next prompt, and follow for more tips taken straight from the official AI guides.
